question: The article ‘S-INFO: how anti-abortion associations use public funds to expand in Piedmont’s healthcare sector’, published on the website of the S-INFO project1 and picked up by media outlets such as Global Project2, gives a distorted and disparaging account of the work of thirdsector groups to support motherhood.

According to the site, this investigation is part of a project cofinanced by the European Education and Culture Executive Agency (EACEA). The ‘Vita nascente’ fund in the Region of Piedmont, established by Article 19 of Regional Law 6/2022, finances social welfare measures to promote motherhood under regional competences.

It is therefore a serious matter that EU funds are being used to support a media initiative that not only undermines activities recognised under regional law, but also discredits institutional action by the Region of Piedmont, disrupting the appropriate balance between the European Union and regional autonomy. In view of this: 1.
Can the Commission confirm that this project receives funding from the EACEA?

Does it consider that the use of EU funds for initiatives that attack legitimately adopted regional policies is compatible with the principles of impartiality, pluralism and respect for institutional competences?
How will it strengthen its oversight to ensure that European resources are not used for campaigns that discredit institutions?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.2.2026) The project S-Info has indeed received co-funding from Creative Europe cross-sectoral strand, following an open call for proposals supporting news media projects1. The EU budget aims to enhance professional journalism and does not support campaigns.

This call follows strict, transparent and pre-established criteria to select projects that redistribute funds to a wide range of smaller media projects, with an aim to enhance media pluralism. Beneficiaries operate with editorial independence further to the grant award and the grant agreements contain safeguards for editorial independence from any donor.

At the same time, applicants commit to professional standards, including by providing multiple and plural viewpoints and by upholding media pluralism. The Commission does not have a role in editorial decisions taken by the beneficiaries but monitors support to media projects from technical and financial perspectives in close cooperation with the European Education and Culture Executive Agency.
All the provisions of our contracts must be respected, in line with the Financial Regulation.
